analysis.title: Economic Outlook: November 2026
key_insights: Midterm elections did not materially change the outlook. Full-year GDP growth is forecast at 2.4% for 2026 and 2.5% for 2027, essentially unchanged from October. Recent equity volatility and a possible tighter regulatory environment for the AI buildout are modest downside risks to spending and investment.
The AI buildout stays intact but is set to slow. Power and compute supply constraints imply a more moderate pace of growth in AI-related business fixed investment even with strong demand.
Labor market expected to stay broadly in balance. Payrolls are forecast to average 65k per month in 2027, in line with breakeven job growth, keeping the unemployment rate steady at 4.1% through 2027.

Core PCE forecast raised slightly to 3.3% y/y in Q4-26 after a hot October CPI. Core inflation is expected to ease to 2.6% y/y in Q4-27 as tariff effects fade and AI-related goods demand cools, while core services stay sticky.

FOMC has shifted hawkish. Base case is a 25 bp hike in December followed by an extended hold through 2027, with risks tilted toward 1-2 more hikes early in 2027. Wells Fargo calls a December hike a lock unless financial conditions deteriorate sharply.
October core CPI came in about 8 bps above consensus at 0.3%. A 0.4% core PCE print is plausible depending on PPI. The data reset the clock on the Fed seeing several good inflation prints in a row.
Year-end 2027 10-year Treasury yield forecast is 4.85%. The fed funds upper bound is projected at 4.25% from Q4-26 through 2027, from 4.00% currently.

Consumer spending has held up despite higher gasoline costs. Real consumption growth is expected above 2% in Q4 and roughly matching this year's pace in 2027, supported by income revisions and household wealth.

Q3 equipment spending was stronger than expected, and structures investment accelerated on data centers and power. New regulations may slow data center starts, but the existing pipeline supports healthy structures investment through 2027.
Residential investment is still pressured by mortgage rates above 7.0% and weak buyer demand. Single-family permits are moderating while multifamily permits have picked up modestly.
Net exports are a persistent drag. A surge in imports of high-tech goods subtracted more than 3 percentage points from Q3 GDP growth, and continued high-tech investment should keep imports elevated.

Fiscal: a budget reconciliation bill or debt ceiling resolution is unlikely in the lame duck session, and the December 11 funding deadline is likely punted to Q1 or early Q2 by a continuing resolution. FY2027 deficit is projected at $2.0 trillion (about 6% of GDP). Treasury is expected to hit the debt ceiling around early March, with an X date around early Q4 2027.

Global tightening cycle is extending into 2027: ECB 25 bp hike in December is the base case (risk of a later move), BoE hiked in November with another 25 bp expected in Q1-27, BoC is expected to hike at consecutive meetings to 3.00% by Q1-27, BoJ is expected to hike in December and again in 2027 to 1.75%.

Emerging markets have turned more hawkish. RBI's second hike is brought forward to December 2026, Brazil cuts are pushed to Q2 2027, Banxico is expected to hold at 6.25% after a larger-than-expected cut, and China is the exception with more easing scope in 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Mortgage rates above 7.0% and weak buyer demand keep pressure on home sales and single-family construction. A floor is expected from modestly lower rates and a stabilizing apartment market.
Data center and power construction drove the Q3 structures acceleration, and the project pipeline supports investment through 2027, though supply constraints slow the pace of growth.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Growth outlook unchanged from October despite midterm results, which supports a sturdy-growth backdrop.
Near-term forecast nudged higher after the hot October CPI. Inflation stays above the Fed's 2% target through 2027.
Latest printed core PCE level, per the report's chart annotation.
Upside surprise that put the FOMC hawks back in the driver's seat.
A December 25 bp hike is the base case, then an extended hold, with risk of 1-2 more hikes early in 2027.
Roughly equal to breakeven job growth, enough to hold the unemployment rate steady.
Consistent with labor market conditions near full employment.
Gradual decline from the current 5.10% as inflation cools.
Little change in the fiscal impulse is expected under divided government.
Keeps home sales and single-family construction under pressure.
Permits remain in a low gear.

risk_factors: Energy price outlook is highly uncertain and is the largest swing factor for inflation.
Hiking cycles have an inertial component, and the recent inflation data create upside risk to the 2027 fed funds path (1-2 more hikes early next year).
A tighter regulatory environment around the AI buildout could slow data center starts and business investment.
Equity market volatility could weigh on consumer spending.
Financial conditions could deteriorate enough to derail the December hike.
Debt ceiling is expected to bind around early March 2027 under a divided government.
Higher global government bond yields keep financial conditions tight, and delayed pass-through and second-round effects could keep inflation elevated.

tension_points.bull_case: Wells Fargo's base case is a December 25 bp hike then an extended hold through 2027, with core inflation cooling gradually and no clear signs of demand-side inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: Hiking cycles have inertia, the October inflation data reset the clock on several good prints in a row, and risks are tilted toward 1-2 more hikes early in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further hot inflation data, such as a 0.4% core PCE print, would push toward additional hikes. A sharp deterioration in financial conditions could derail the December hike.
